title: FOS Knockdown Alleviates Helicobacter pylori-Infected Gastritis by Suppressing Mast Cell Activation and Treg Polarization.
authors: Ma, Wen; Han, Ruidong; Wang, Lei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究FOS敲低对幽门螺杆菌胃炎中肥大细胞和Treg极化的影响，属纯湿实验与表达分析，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Helicobacter pylori (HP) is a major cause of gastritis, yet the epithelial mechanisms linking infection-induced stress to mast cell and Treg responses remain poorly defined. METHODS: Three datasets (GSE5081, GSE27411, and GSE233973) were integrated and analyzed using weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and machine learning algorithms. Mast cell-related hub gene expressions were evaluated with quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), and inflammatory cytokines were quantified using the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Histopathological changes were evaluated using hematoxylin and eosin (HE), Giemsa, and Warthin-Starry silver staining. Cell apoptosis was assessed by flow cytometry, and mast cell and Treg cell activities were analyzed by Transwell assays, histamine detection, and immunohistochemistry (IHC). RESULTS: Fos proto-oncogene (FOS), ribonucleotide reductase regulatory subunit M2 (RRM2), and RAD51 recombinase (RAD51) were identified as mast cell-related hub genes, all of which were upregulated in HP-induced gastritis mice. In vitro, HP infection or CagA stimulation increased FOS expression in gastric epithelial cells. FOS knockdown in HP-infected mice alleviated gastric mucosal injury, reduced bacterial burden, and decreased pro-inflammatory cytokine levels. FOS silencing enhanced GES-1 cell viability and suppressed apoptosis. In HP-infected GES-1 cells, FOS silencing inhibited mast cell migration, cytokine secretion, including C-C motif chemokine ligand 2 (CCL2), interleukin-33 (IL-33), and stem cell factor (SCF), as well as histamine release, accompanied by reduced Treg polarization and decreased expression of transforming growth factor-beta and forkhead box P3. CONCLUSION: FOS silencing inhibited mast cell activation and Treg cell polarization in HP-induced gastritis, suggesting its promising value as an intervention point in HP-driven gastritis.
abstract_zh: 背景：幽门螺杆菌（Helicobacter pylori, HP）是胃炎的主要病因，但感染诱导的应激与肥大细胞及调节性T细胞（Treg）反应之间的上皮机制仍不明确。方法：整合并分析了三个数据集（GSE5081、GSE27411和GSE233973），采用加权基因共表达网络分析（WGCNA）和机器学习算法。通过实时定量聚合酶链反应（qRT-PCR）评估肥大细胞相关核心基因表达，并使用酶联免疫吸附测定（ELISA）定量炎症细胞因子。组织病理学变化通过苏木精-伊红（HE）、吉姆萨（Giemsa）和Warthin-Starry银染评估。细胞凋亡通过流式细胞术检测，肥大细胞和Treg细胞活性通过Transwell实验、组胺检测和免疫组织化学（IHC）分析。结果：Fos原癌基因（FOS）、核糖核苷酸还原酶调节亚基M2（RRM2）和RAD51重组酶（RAD51）被鉴定为肥大细胞相关核心基因，这些基因在HP诱导的胃炎小鼠中均上调。体外实验中，HP感染或CagA刺激增加了胃上皮细胞中FOS的表达。在HP感染小鼠中，FOS敲低减轻了胃黏膜损伤，降低了细菌负荷，并减少了促炎细胞因子水平。FOS沉默增强了GES-1细胞活力并抑制了凋亡。在HP感染的GES-1细胞中，FOS沉默抑制了肥大细胞迁移、细胞因子分泌（包括C-C基序趋化因子配体2（CCL2）、白细胞介素-33（IL-33）和干细胞因子（SCF））以及组胺释放，同时伴随Treg极化减少和转化生长因子-β及叉头框蛋白P3表达降低。结论：FOS沉默抑制了HP诱导胃炎中的肥大细胞活化和Treg细胞极化，表明其作为HP驱动胃炎干预靶点的潜在价值。
